To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the storage costs of query-based sampled documents can be reduced by pruning the documents to a small subset of sentences, that the storage costs can be further reduced by pruning the sentences to a small set of terms and that the resulting pruned documents are accurate enough for federated search.
the disk storage costs of sampled documents can be reduced by a factor of three while causing only minor loss in federated search quality.
query-based sampling is a promising technique for discovering the content of uncooperative text databases but disk storage costs can become surprisingly high.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical problem of reducing disk storage costs for query-based sampling of large documents.
the problem of reducing storage costs for query-based sampling of uncooperative text databases.
the practical issues of creating and managing a federated search service in environments containing many independent text search engines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pruning is a useful technique to reduce disk storage costs for query-based sampling.

query-based sampling is an effective method for creating database resource descriptions that can be used to support federated searching, but that the storage costs of sampled documents can be reduced significantly while causing only minor decreases in federated search performance.
query-based sampling with document pruning can be a useful technique for reducing storage costs when federated searching many text databases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
federated search can be performed at very low storage costs.
the query-based sampling method can be used to discover and represent the contents of text databases in a federated search environment without incurring prohibitive disk storage costs.
federated search systems can be built at a lower cost when query-based sampling is used to obtain resource descriptions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the costs of sampling and storing documents can be greatly reduced by using a pruning strategy based on the document length.
query-based sampling is an effective approach to creating database resource descriptions for text databases, even in environments where disk storage costs are a concern.
the costs of federated search systems can be reduced by pruning the documents obtained by sampling.
